notes: Times are wall-clock microseconds (std::chrono::steady_clock) around the stated interval. Every interval that uses the device ends after cudaStreamSynchronize, except empty_kernel_launch_no_sync. Percentiles interpolate linearly between order statistics.

Each measurement runs warm-up iterations first, then 'reps' repetitions. The count is the default in 'harness' unless that many repetitions would exceed the time budget; then it is budget / iteration time, and at least min_repetitions.
One user stream (cudaStreamCreate), default scheduling flag (cudaDeviceScheduleAuto), one host thread.

library: variant rmm_pool uses rmm::exec_policy_nosync with a pool memory resource for Thrust temporaries; variant cuda_malloc uses thrust::cuda::par_nosync, whose temporaries come from cudaMalloc. Both are followed by cudaStreamSynchronize inside the interval. reduce_by_key has one key per 16 elements; copy_if keeps about 10% (exact count in 'kept'); every sort repetition starts from the same unsorted input, restored outside the interval.
Sizes are binary (1 MB = 2^20 bytes) and gb_per_s uses 2^30 bytes. Pageable copies use cudaMemcpyAsync on the same stream followed by a synchronisation, like the pinned ones.
allocation: cudaHostAlloc with cudaHostAllocDefault. The rmm pool is created once with a fixed size before the measurements, so pool growth is never inside an interval.

dirty_list: a record is 24 bytes (int index, int pad, 16-byte value); the state array has 1e7 16-byte values (1e6 in quick mode); indices are random and distinct. host_to_device = the host fills k records into a pinned buffer (phase host_fill), one copy, one scatter kernel, synchronise. host_fill reads each value from a random position of a host copy of the state array, so above about 1e3 records it is mostly host cache misses and not the write into the pinned buffer; copy_scatter_sync is the device part. device_to_host has three variants. flag_scan_atomic: one kernel over all changed flags of the state array with an integer atomic slot counter (record order not deterministic). flag_scan_ordered: cub::DeviceSelect::Flagged over the same flags with preallocated temporary storage, count read back, one gather kernel (deterministic order). frontier_emit_atomic: one kernel over a device list of the k candidate indices with an atomic slot counter. Each variant reads the count back to pinned memory, then copies count records to pinned memory.

gather: random CSR generated on the device (row lengths uniform in 4..64, 32-bit column ids, double values, 64-bit offsets). The frontier is a random set of distinct rows whose total length is the largest not above the size label. gather_rows_to_host = transform_exclusive_scan of the frontier row lengths, one gather kernel into one contiguous buffer (offsets, values, column ids), count read back (phase scan_gather_count), one copy of the buffer to pinned memory (phase copy_buffer). The three variants are one kernel with different launch shapes. thread_per_row copies each row serially in one thread, 256 rows per block; thread_per_row_block_32 does the same with 32 rows per block; warp_per_row spreads each row over the 32 threads of one warp, 8 rows per block. In the one-thread-per-row variants a warp works on 32 different rows at once, and the time depends on the block size, not only on the row lengths. frontier_upload is the separate cost of sending the frontier row ids from pinned memory and is not part of gather_rows_to_host.

unified_memory: cudaMallocManaged on an x86 node with a discrete GPU. Every hand-over between host and device is served by page faults and page migration. This is NOT the Grace Hopper behaviour and must not be used to estimate it. The reference rows give the same host loop on pinned memory and the same kernel on device memory.
